System A:
  Clarity: 8.2/10
  Engagement: 8.0/10
  Depth Appropriateness: 8.3/10
  Breadth: 8.5/10
System B:
  Clarity: 7.8/10
  Engagement: 7.5/10
  Depth Appropriateness: 8.0/10
  Breadth: 8.2/10
System C:
  Clarity: 7.5/10
  Engagement: 6.8/10
  Depth Appropriateness: 6.5/10
  Breadth: 7.0/10

Explanation:
[A|Clarity] In the warm-start dialogue, the Background discussion expert explains the cold-start fix with concrete mechanisms: "the platform pushes new videos to users flagged as domain-savvy based on their prior substantive comments, and those referees' likes, saves, watch time, and in-depth comments carry higher weight" — a clear, example-grounded explanation of an otherwise opaque mechanism. The final summary also explains the recommendation priority formula in plain terms ("comprehensive predicted user behavior probability × behavior value weight = video recommendation priority"). Minor gap: some transitions between the micro-drama iteration cases and the algorithmic explanation rely on the reader connecting "the algorithm can't register the moment audiences feel offended" to the earlier formula discussion without an explicit bridge.

[A|Engagement] The moderator's questions are framed to draw the user into a live tension, e.g., "how did niche, vertical content ever stand a chance in that random-audience cold-start pool, and what exactly has the platform changed to give specialized creators a fairer shot?" — this positions the user as an insider facing a real problem. The expert answers then close with a pointed question back to the table ("how do creators tell the difference between listening and chasing?"), sustaining involvement. Gap: the user's own later prompts are brief topic restatements rather than substantive contributions, so the sense of co-direction is partly simulated by the moderator role rather than driven by the user.

[A|Depth Appropriateness] The progression from the general dissemination loop (Round 1) to the specific cold-start mechanism (Round 2) to the implicit/explicit signal weighting (Round 3, Platform algorithm engineer) builds coherently. The engineer's contribution adds appropriate technical depth — "Wide&Deep, Two-Tower... trained on historical behaviour data, not content/tag matching" — without overwhelming the earlier, more accessible framing. The final summary flags genuine limits ("Exact functional forms and weights aren't public; the formula is a simplification with fictitious illustrative numbers"), which is well-judged honesty about depth boundaries.

[A|Breadth] The final summary covers algorithmic recommendation, audience feedback signals, creator adaptation, cold-start for niche content, comment-data authenticity, and implicit/explicit signal weighting — a genuinely multidimensional treatment. The connection between the "content referee" mechanism and the broader cold-start problem, and between the micro-drama iteration cases and the algorithmic weighting discussion, are explicitly drawn. Gap: the privacy/ethics dimension of large-scale audio-visual analytics is not developed, and cross-platform generalization is only implied.

[B|Clarity] The instructor's answers explain the confound structure well: "When you observe that videos with energetic music or fast cuts get more shares on Douyin, it is tempting to read that as 'these features cause sharing.' That reading is usually wrong... because two very different engines are running at once." The fusion trade-off is also explained concretely ("Early fusion can capture cross-modal interactions... but it is fragile when a modality is missing or noisy"). Gap: some of the identification-strategy vocabulary (e.g., "switchback or cluster designs to absorb network spillover") is named without sufficient unpacking for a reader who has not encountered causal-inference methodology.

[B|Engagement] The student's selected questions are well-motivated and the instructor answers them directly, e.g., the creator-adaptation question is answered with a concrete loop ("post a video with a trending track, fast cuts, and bold on-screen text, then watch the comment section and share counts, and revise"). The extension sections ("A closely related idea is the distinction between explicit and implicit feedback signals") give the user a productive next thread. Gap: the user's guidance in later rounds is again a restatement of the topic rather than a substantive contribution, so the sense of the user steering the investigation is limited.

[B|Depth Appropriateness] The progression from confound identification (Round 1) to creator adaptation and implicit/explicit feedback (Round 2) to generalization across tiers and interface signals (Round 3) is coherent and appropriately deepens. The exposure-normalization point is developed with a concrete reason ("the denominator encodes an assumption about who was eligible to react"). The final summary honestly flags unresolved items ("Early-vs-late fusion for shares vs. comments is unresolved and confounded by exposure"). Gap: some of the more technical identification strategies are named at a level of generality that may exceed what the user's stated goal requires.

[B|Breadth] The final summary covers multimodal feature extraction, the algorithmic-push vs. audience-pull confound, fusion strategy, creator adaptation, implicit vs. explicit feedback, generalization across creator tiers and genres, interface signals, and ethics — a well-developed set of perspectives with explicit relationships (e.g., "Interface signals are confounds/moderators; test with content-held-constant A/B designs"). The tier/genre generalization discussion adds a genuinely important boundary condition. Gap: the treatment of actual Douyin platform mechanisms (as opposed to generic short-video platform mechanisms) is thinner than in System A, since System B's evidence base is more methodological than platform-specific.

[C|Clarity] The answers are well-structured and the comment typology is clearly presented in a table ("Dissemination-oriented | Shares/amplifies content... Attitudinal | Expresses intention to visit... Informational | Asks questions or offers suggestions"). The visibility–responsiveness framework is explained in accessible terms. Gap: some transitions between rounds — particularly the shift from the Xi'an comment typology to the thinspiration study in Round 3 — are not explicitly motivated, and the reader must reconstruct why the topic shift is relevant.

[C|Engagement] The answers are informative but largely expository; the user's prompts are brief topic restatements or a generic "What else should I know about this topic?" The system does not actively draw the user into a task or pose productive questions that would sustain involvement. The final summary is a consolidation rather than an invitation to continue. Gap: there is little evidence of the system responding to user contributions or using the user's specific intent to shape the direction of exploration.

[C|Depth Appropriateness] The explanations are at a survey level — the frameworks are named and briefly described, but the mechanisms (e.g., how the recommendation system actually allocates visibility, how the P_k balance is computed) are not developed. The final summary's open questions are listed but not explored. For a user whose intent is "to analyze how audio-visual content is shared on Douyin and understand the mechanisms of audience feedback," this level of depth is useful as an orientation but insufficient for the stated analytical goal. Gap: the "mechanisms" the user asked about are described at a conceptual level rather than a mechanistic one.

[C|Breadth] The three rounds cover the BSU thesis framing, the tuwei ecology visibility analysis, the Xi'an comment typology, the visibility–responsiveness framework, multimodal feature analysis (thinspiration study), and nonverbal cue research — a reasonable spread of perspectives. The relationships among them are partly drawn (e.g., "Xu's framework provides the communication-theoretic description of this loop, Feng et al. supply its socio-technical mechanism"). Gap: the breadth is more enumerative than relational; several perspectives are named and briefly described but not developed enough for the user to understand why they matter in relation to each other, and the ethical/domain-sensitivity dimension is flagged but not developed.
